introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Carry out the following formatting instructions.

i. Add horizontal borders for the cells in the ranges A3:E3 and A16:E16  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **A3:E3**, hold **Ctrl** and select **A16:E16** (the two heading rows, *Expenses* and *Income*). *Home* > **Borders** > **Top and Bottom Border** (or *All Borders*): a horizontal line frames each heading row.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the two ranges selected (1); horizontal borders applied (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: ii. Merge the cells in the range A1:E1  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **A1:E1** and click **Merge & Center**: the heading BUDGET FOR THE TERM is in one wide cell.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* A1:E1 merged.

questions.enonce_markdown: iii. Format the heading to Bold and a size of 20 points  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Click the merged heading cell, click **Bold** (Ctrl+B) and choose **20** in the *Font Size* box.

*Marking idea (1 mark):* bold and 20 points.

questions.enonce_markdown: iv. Format the cells in the range B4:E21 to use the thousands separator and zero decimal place when displaying numbers  *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **B4:E21**, then *Home* > *Format Cells* > *Number* > **Number**: **Decimal places: 0** and tick **Use 1000 Separator (,)** (or use the **Comma Style** button and *Decrease Decimal* twice). The amounts then appear as 150,000, 20,000, 200,000 and so on, with no decimals. The range includes the empty cells of the total column, so that the totals computed in questions 4 to 6 are formatted too.

*Marking idea (4 marks):* range B4:E21 selected (2); thousands separator (1); zero decimal places (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: v. Set the horizontal alignment of Cells B23:E23 to Centre.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **B23:E23** and click **Center** (*Home* > *Alignment*), or *Format Cells* > *Alignment* > *Horizontal: Center*. The comment that the IF formula displays in row 23 is then centred.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* B23:E23 selected (1); centre alignment (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the Sum function at Cell E4 to sum the contents of the cell range B4:D4. Copy the formula down to Cell E11, and also to Cells E17 to E19 and Cell E21.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**E4: `=SUM(B4:D4)`**

Drag the fill handle of E4 down to **E11**. Then copy E4 (Ctrl+C) and paste it (Ctrl+V) into **E17:E19** and into **E21**; each pasted formula adjusts to its own row: E17 is `=SUM(B17:D17)`, E18 is `=SUM(B18:D18)`, E19 is `=SUM(B19:D19)`, E21 is `=SUM(B21:D21)`.

Results (recalculated with Python): E4 to E11 = 150000, 20000, 45000, 6000, 1500, 75000, 15000, 20000; E17 = 200000; E18 = 75000; E19 = 77500; E21 = 352500 (250,000 + 50,000 + 52,500).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* SUM function with the range B4:D4 (1); copied down to E11 (1); copied to E17:E19 and E21 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Compute the Jan expenses in Cell B13. Copy the formula in Cells C13 and D13 to do the computation of expenses for Feb and Mar.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**B13: `=SUM(B4:B11)`** = 222,500 (150000 + 20000 + 15000 + 2000 + 500 + 25000 + 5000 + 5000).

Copy B13 to **C13** (`=SUM(C4:C11)` = 57,500) and **D13** (`=SUM(D4:D11)` = 52,500). The School Fees and Books cells of February and March are empty, so they add nothing.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* formula for Jan (1); copied to C13 and D13 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Compute the Jan income in Cell B21. Copy the formula in Cells C21 and D21 to do the computation of expenses for Feb and Mar.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The income of January is the sum of the three income lines of column B:

**B21: `=SUM(B17:B19)`** = 250,000 (200000 + 25000 + 25000)

Copy B21 to **C21** (`=SUM(C17:C19)` = 50,000) and **D21** (`=SUM(D17:D19)` = 52,500). (The sentence of the paper says *expenses* for Feb and Mar; the cells C21 and D21 are of course the *income* of those months.)

*Marking idea (2 marks):* formula for Jan income (1); copied to C21 and D21 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Use the IF function at Cell B23 to display the message **Good** if the expenses for Jan are less than or equal to income for Jan, otherwise, display the message **Bad**.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Compare the expenses of January (B13) with the income of January (B21); the messages are text, so they are in double quotation marks:

**B23: `=IF(B13<=B21,"Good","Bad")`**

Value: 222,500 <= 250,000 is true, so B23 displays **Good**. Copied to C23 and D23 the formula gives **Bad** for February (57,500 > 50,000) and **Good** for March (52,500 <= 52,500, the equality case counts as Good).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* IF function with the test B13<=B21 (1); Good in quotation marks as the true value (1); Bad as the false value (1).
